gen-dafont-jelly-crazies-gf-arimo: Wobbly, tube-like letters with bowls nearly sealed shut take the heading, and Jelly Crazies keeps that stroke the same all the way round. Arimo sits beneath in sans-serif with open, rounded terminals.
gen-dafont-jelly-crazies-gf-armata: Squishy and playful, Jelly Crazies closes its bowls almost completely and slows the eye to a stroll. Armata, a contemporary sans, opens everything back up.
gen-dafont-jelly-crazies-gf-athiti: Athiti has a high mean line and an s you can see straight through, which makes it friendly and light under Jelly Crazies. Its wobbly, nearly sealed shapes get the spotlight up top.
gen-dafont-jelly-crazies-gf-atkinson-hyp: Jelly Crazies draws its letters like outlines traced in a single width, wobbly and nearly sealed at the bowls. Atkinson Hyperlegible follows in a plain sans with wide-set s terminals, so a long passage moves along smoothly, with only slightly clipped capitals.

Atkinson Hyperlegible Mono spaces its letters far apart, like stencil bridges stretched open, with counters that breathe. And Jelly Crazies, wobbly and nearly closed, gives the page its playful, slow-walking headline.
Atkinson Hyperlegible Next reads approachably, its lowercase eyes big as washers and its rounds left unlatched like a hook. Jelly Crazies adds wobbly, same-width terminals above.
gen-dafont-jelly-crazies-gf-biryani: Jelly Crazies wobbles with a tube-like stroke and bowls that almost seal, never thinning the way a pen would. Biryani, a sans-serif with big-eyed e shapes and unclogged counters, keeps a long read clear.
gen-dafont-jelly-crazies-gf-blinker: Blinker reads clean and approachable, with open apertures and lowercase that fills most of its height. Jelly Crazies does goofy, nearly closed wobble best; Blinker does steady text best.
gen-dafont-jelly-crazies-gf-carrois-goth: Playful from the first letter, Jelly Crazies wobbles with nearly sealed bowls while Carrois Gothic opens its c generously. Its high x-height holds up well at modest sizes, and the heading can go bigger.

Carrois Gothic SC reads in a contemporary, approachable way, with clear openings at every curve and capitals barely taller than lowercase. Jelly Crazies wobbles above it, its closed, thin-looking letters loosening up the whole page.
